scenes.section: A private company runs Medicare for you

lines.raw: With **Medicare Advantage** (also called **Part C** or **MA**), a person still has Medicare, but a **private insurance company** handles their care.
lines.say: With Medicare Advantage (also called Part C or M A), a person still has Medicare, but a private insurance company handles their care.

lines.raw: The insurer must cover everything Parts A and B cover, and most MA plans also include **Part D** drug cover.
lines.say: The insurer must cover everything Parts A and B cover, and most M A plans also include Part D drug cover.

lines.raw: In 2025, a little **over half** of people on Medicare are in an MA plan.
lines.say: In 2025, a little over half of people on Medicare are in an M A plan.

scenes.section: A private company runs Medicare for you

lines.raw: Think of an office canteen contractor.
lines.say: Think of an office canteen contractor.

lines.raw: A company could run its own staff canteen, buying every kilo of rice and paying every cook.
lines.say: A company could run its own staff canteen, buying every kilo of rice and paying every cook.

lines.raw: Or it could hire a **contractor** and pay a fixed **amount per employee per month**.
lines.say: Or it could hire a contractor and pay a fixed amount per employee per month.

lines.raw: The contractor must serve at least the agreed meals.
lines.say: The contractor must serve at least the agreed meals.

lines.raw: If it runs the kitchen cheaply and well, it keeps the difference, and it may add tea and biscuits to attract staff.
lines.say: If it runs the kitchen cheaply and well, it keeps the difference, and it may add tea and biscuits to attract staff.

lines.raw: Medicare is the company, the MA insurer is the contractor, and the fixed amount is called a **capitation** payment.
lines.say: Medicare is the company, the M A insurer is the contractor, and the fixed amount is called a capitation payment.

lines.raw: Original Medicare vs Medicare Advantage.
lines.say: Original Medicare versus Medicare Advantage.

lines.raw: Who pays the doctor? Original Medicare (A + B): The government, through a MAC. Medicare Advantage (C): The private MA plan.
lines.say: Who pays the doctor? Original Medicare (A and B): The government, through a M A C. Medicare Advantage (C): The private M A plan.

lines.raw: Which doctors? Original Medicare (A + B): Almost any doctor in the US who takes Medicare. Medicare Advantage (C): Usually a **network** of doctors and hospitals.
lines.say: Which doctors? Original Medicare (A and B): Almost any doctor in the U S who takes Medicare. Medicare Advantage (C): Usually a network of doctors and hospitals.

lines.raw: Referrals and approvals. Original Medicare (A + B): Rarely needed. Medicare Advantage (C): Often needed: referrals (HMOs) and **prior authorisation**.
lines.say: Referrals and approvals. Original Medicare (A and B): Rarely needed. Medicare Advantage (C): Often needed: referrals (H M O's) and prior authorisation.

lines.raw: Drug cover. Original Medicare (A + B): Buy a separate Part D plan. Medicare Advantage (C): Usually built in (an **MA-PD** plan).
lines.say: Drug cover. Original Medicare (A and B): Buy a separate Part D plan. Medicare Advantage (C): Usually built in (an M A PD plan).

lines.raw: Extras (dental, vision, hearing, gym). Original Medicare (A + B): Mostly not covered. Medicare Advantage (C): Often included.
lines.say: Extras (dental, vision, hearing, gym). Original Medicare (A and B): Mostly not covered. Medicare Advantage (C): Often included.

lines.raw: Yearly out-of-pocket limit. Original Medicare (A + B): None. Medicare Advantage (C): Yes: at most **$9,350** for in-network care in 2025, often lower.
lines.say: Yearly out-of-pocket limit. Original Medicare (A and B): None. Medicare Advantage (C): Yes: at most 9350 dollars for in-network care in 2025, often lower.

lines.raw: Can add Medigap? Original Medicare (A + B): Yes. Medicare Advantage (C): No.
lines.say: Can add Medigap? Original Medicare (A and B): Yes. Medicare Advantage (C): No.

scenes.section: How the plan is paid, in one line

lines.raw: CMS pays each MA plan a fixed amount **per member per month** (a **capitation** payment), set higher for members who are expected to cost more because of their health.
lines.say: C M S pays each M A plan a fixed amount per member per month (a capitation payment), set higher for members who are expected to cost more because of their health.

lines.raw: For Robert, his plan receives about **$1,265 a month** (an illustrative figure).
lines.say: For Robert, his plan receives about 1265 dollars a month (an illustrative figure).

lines.raw: Doctors and hospitals then bill the **plan**, not Medicare, and the plan sends CMS a copy of each service as **encounter data**.
lines.say: Doctors and hospitals then bill the plan, not Medicare, and the plan sends C M S a copy of each service as encounter data.

scenes.section: How the plan is paid, in one line

lines.raw: How the payment is worked out.
lines.say: How the payment is worked out.

lines.raw: The monthly amount is adjusted by each member's **risk score**, which is built from the diagnosis codes on their claims and encounters.
lines.say: The monthly amount is adjusted by each member's risk score, which is built from the diagnosis codes on their claims and encounters.

lines.raw: That is why MA plans care so much about complete, accurate coding.
lines.say: That is why M A plans care so much about complete, accurate coding.

lines.raw: The Risk Adjustment course explains the full method.
lines.say: The Risk Adjustment course explains the full method.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **HMO**. How it works: Use the plan's network; usually need a primary care doctor and referrals to see specialists. Out-of-network care is not covered except emergencies.
lines.say: H M O. How it works: Use the plan's network; usually need a primary care doctor and referrals to see specialists. Out-of-network care is not covered except emergencies.

lines.raw: **PPO**. How it works: Can go out of network, but pay more for it.
lines.say: P P O. How it works: Can go out of network, but pay more for it.

lines.raw: **SNP** (Special Needs Plan). How it works: For specific groups: people with both Medicare and Medicaid (**D-SNP**), certain chronic conditions (**C-SNP**), or living in a nursing home (**I-SNP**).
lines.say: S N P (Special Needs Plan). How it works: For specific groups: people with both Medicare and Medicaid (D-SNP), certain chronic conditions (C-SNP), or living in a nursing home (I-SNP).

lines.raw: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Medicare Advantage (Part C) is Medicare delivered by private insurers approved by CMS.
